views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold the current tariff posture and actively re-engage the negotiating channel rather than escalating further. The Sept 1 List 4 escalation and any further hikes should be treated as leverage to be traded, not as policy automatically pursued; instead signal a concrete, time-limited offer to de-escalate in exchange for verifiable enforcement and purchase commitments, while keeping the threat of the scheduled tariffs on the table as the counterweight.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat reading is elevated but not existential — roughly +0.45 by the US anchors. The US retains leverage (dollar strong at 117.9 on the broad index, industrial production up, CPI contained at 256), so this is not a survival-level threat. However, the recession-risk signal is now material and cannot be dismissed: the 10Y/2Y curve inverted repeatedly through late August (10Y at 1.47 vs 2Y at 1.50 by Aug 28), consumer sentiment crashed from 100 in May to 89.8 in August, and the Fed has already cut to 2.13% and is signaling further easing (CNBC/PBS, Aug 14-23). That is the market explicitly warning that this escalation spiral risks recession. Against that backdrop, the Aug 23 decision to push List 4 to 15% and direct firms to exit China invites exactly the mutually-damaging response China has been showing with its $75B retaliation and auto-tariff resumption. The action stance therefore is mild: hold/negotiate around +0.15. Escalating further turns a manageable, leverage-rich dispute into a recession risk with no offsetting concession; a full rollback would forfeit hard-won leverage with no matching commitment on enforcement. Negotiating from strength — using the scheduled tariffs as the credible threat while offering an off-ramp — is the posture that protects US supply chains and growth without throwing away the leverage the US has built.

Fed already cut to 2.13%; dollar strength (117.9) shows robust US leverage
China retaliation accelerating ($75B new tariffs + auto tariff resumption on Aug 23)
Aug 23 US decision to raise List 4 to 15% and direct firms to exit China — high risk of escalation spiral
US fundamentals still firm (IP up, low CPI), so threat is elevated but not existential
